title: Runtime Reliability & Data Truth
documentationIdentityRule: The current package/build/QA identity is owned by release_identity.json, this release contract, VERSION.txt/app bootstrap and the last-loaded v18.7 release identity overlay. Long-form README and bundled user/developer/limitations documents retain historical release narrative and canonical headings; they are not rewritten solely to duplicate release identity metadata.
legacyPlanRule: Historical certification_plan.json and ci_pipeline_plan.json remain conserved legacy registries. v18.7 current execution authority is the three canonical GitHub workflows plus this release contract and run_full_certification.sh; do not cosmetically rewrite the legacy registries merely to change their version label.
releaseRecoveryRule: If the single canonical Release run fails because a pre-existing release-harness/gate assumption contradicts the frozen release contract, do not rerun unchanged evidence. Recreate the same v18.7.0-development line from the failed merged candidate, fix only the proven release-harness defect, require fresh exact-head Fast + full Qualified, and re-enter the same canonical G11-G16 Release workflow through a merged development PR. No retry/certification/promotion branch or extra workflow is permitted.
qualificationRule: Exact-head Fast and full Qualified, including backend/race/randomized, renderer, Chrome and WebKit, must PASS before merge. G12 then re-certifies the exact merged candidate without replacing pre-merge WebKit evidence.
releaseRule: Normal path is one development branch, one PR, one immutable merged candidate, one G11-G16 Stable release run; no retry/certification/promotion branches. A proven post-merge release-harness defect follows releaseRecoveryRule rather than an unchanged-SHA rerun.
requiredV1870Evidence: bounded provider pressure and load-SLO behavior
